chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washsha from Hammad ibn Uthman from Ibn Abi Yafur who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the man who is in a state of major ritual impurity (junub) and with him is water sufficient only for his drinking. Should he perform Tayammum or Wudu? He (peace be upon him) said: 'Tayammum is superior. Do you not see that only half the purification has been made obligatory upon him?'

key_terms.نِصْفُ الطَّهُورِ: Half the purification, referring to the reduced water requirement for Tayammum compared to Wudu
key_terms.يَتَوَضَّأُ: To perform Wudu, minor ablution using water
key_terms.يُجْنِبُ: To be in a state of major ritual impurity (junub)

ai.seo_question: What should a person do if they are ritually impure and have only enough water for drinking?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes the principle of preserving life and health over ritual perfection when resources are critically scarce, ruling that a junub individual with water sufficient only for drinking should perform Tayammum to avoid dehydration. The Imam justifies this by noting that Tayammum is 'superior' (afdal) in this specific context because it conserves the limited water for consumption, reflecting the Shia juristic emphasis on the hierarchy of necessities (daruriyyat). This ruling highlights the flexibility of Shia fiqh in balancing ritual purity with the preservation of life, a key theme in Usul al-Fiqh.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad,f rom Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from hammad Bin Usman, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said,

‘I asked Abu Abdullahasws about the man who comes to be with sexual impurity and with him is the water of a measurement of what would suffice him for his drinking. Should he perform Tayammum or an Ablution (Wudhu)?’ Heasws said: ‘The Tayammum is superior. Do you not see that rather half the purification has been made to be upon him?’
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu‘alla’ ibn Muhammad from al-Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from Hammad ibn ‘Uthman from ibn abu Ya‘fur who has said the following:

“I once asked abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about a man who experiences sexual relation and has enough water only for his drinking needs; must he take Tayammum or Wudu’? He (the Imam) said, ‘Tayammum is better. You should understand the fact that the task of cleansing is made only half as much in his favor.’”
